Paragraph:
Translation: As a boat on the water is swept away by a strong wind, even one of the senses on which the mind focuses can carry away a man's intelligence.

Purport (Excerpt): Unless all of the senses are engaged in the service of the Lord, even one of them engaged in sense gratification can deviate the devotee from the path of transcendental advancement...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The vulnerability of an individual who believes they are mostly in control, yet leaves even a single unmanaged impulse unmonitored.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna uses the vivid analogy of a boat being swept off course by a gust of wind. If the mind fixates on even one stray sense object, that single rogue sense can sabotage the entire intellect.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna learns the necessity of comprehensive self-discipline rather than partial effort.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Single-Point Vulnerability: How a single unmonitored habit can ruin overall mental health
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cognitive Distraction: The mind being swept away like a boat in a storm
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.The 'Rogue Impulse': A single stray sense pulling down rational intelligence

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Indriyanam hi caratam (Senses wandering among their objects)
Harati prajnam (Carrying away the discriminating intellect)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Partial surrender leaves a soul vulnerable. Just as a single hole can sink a boat or a single gust of wind drive it off course, allowing even one sense to indulge in material gratification can completely derail a seeker's spiritual progress.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a key metaphor for relapse and distraction. You can have 90% of your life in order, but if you leave one toxic habit, craving, or sensory obsession unmanaged, that single weak link can hijack your prefrontal cortex ('carry away intelligence') and sink your progress like a boat in a gale.
